messages:
Anya: Quick syncI sketched an MVP for letting a single chat request orchestrate multiple tool invocations (parallel + dependencies). Need alignment on ordering, retries, timeouts, and launch gating.

Sam: Yep, paste the sketch and any constraints you already thought through.

Anya: High-level goals: let callers declare a small DAG of tool calls. Runtime executes independent nodes in parallel, respects declared deps, reports structured outputs, and streams model tokens + tool progress. Prioritize read-only tools for beta.

Liam: Nice. Example request body (very rough):
```
POST /v1/chat.complete
{
  \"input\": \"Create a concise summary and pull latest notes for account 123\",
  \"tool_plan\": [
    {\"id\": \"kb\", \"tool\": \"kb_search\", \"args\": {\"q\": \"purchase thread\"}},
    {\"id\": \"notes\", \"tool\": \"get_notes\", \"args\": {\"account_id\": 123}, \"depends_on\": [\"kb\"]}
  ],
  \"overall_timeout_ms\": 6000,
  \"per_call_timeout_ms\": 1200,
  \"on_partial_failure\": \"return_best\" // options: fail, return_best, retry
}
```

Maria: From CS: for auditability we need deterministic, machine-readable ordering and timestamps for each tool call even if executed concurrently. Include correlation ids per call.

Sam: Also: idempotency tokens per plan and a per-tool opt-in for server-side retries. Default: no retries unless tool declares idempotent:true.

Julie: Streaming UX: stream model tokens immediately; also emit small events so frontends can render tool loading/progress and then final tool results embedded in the stream when available.

Liam: Runtime modes idea: mode = fast_fanout (fire all non-dependent calls in parallel) vs safe_serial (serialize where requested). Let user pick per-request or per-subgraph.

Anya: Launch criteria proposal (MVP):
- Support DAG with simple "depends_on" edges (acyclic).
- Per-call timeout and overall request timeout.
- Per-call retry policy (none/once/backoff) with idempotency gating.
- Structured output for each call: {id, tool, start_ts, end_ts, duration_ms, status, attempts, trace_id}.
- Beta supported tools: search, embeddings, rerank, read-only DB reads.
- Beta scale target: up to 5 concurrent calls per request, 50 qps per org on hosted.
- Evals to include race-condition prompts and partial-failure scenarios.

Sam: For retries: default = no automatic retry for non-idempotent tools. Expose retry_policy and require idempotent:true to enable. Retry backoff should be configurable.

Maria: Enterprise ask: some partners require strict ordered execution for billing/charges. Add an explicit atomic flag that forces serialization and fails the whole subgraph on child failure.

Anya: Agreed. Proposal: add atomic:true|false per-subgraph. If atomic and a required call fails, surface a clean error with partial outputs optional for diagnostics.

Liam: Observability: runtime should emit trace/span per tool invocation. Response block must include per-call timing and attempts and a single top-level trace id.

Julie: Streaming events schema (proposal):
- event_type: tool_started | tool_progress | tool_done | model_token
- payload: tool_id, trace_id, snippet_or_token, status
This keeps UI reactive.

Sam: Security notes: sanitize tool args, enforce per-tool rate limits and org scoping to avoid cross-tenant leaks. For Hosted, default conservatism.

Anya: Prioritization and scope: read-only tools first reduces blast radius. Write/side-effectful tools (billing, emails) deferred until we finalize atomic semantics and idempotency guarantees. Also gate enabling at org level in Console for Dedicated/Private.

Maria: +1 from CS for read-only-first. We'll flag the charge/billing serialization as high priority for a few enterprise prospects.

Liam: Performance tradeoffs: parallelism reduces median but can increase tail due to stragglers. Consider offering a \"batchable\":true hint per-tool so runtime can merge similar calls to reduce fanout. Also include opt-out for callers that want predictable latency.

Sam: How should runtime present failures to the model? Two options: (1) inject a synthetic tool result token into the model context (e.g. <tool_result id=notes status=TIMEOUT>), plus structured errors; or (2) keep errors only in response metadata. I prefer (1) so the LM can fallback or ask clarifying questions.

Julie: (UI) We like option (1). It lets chat UI explain missing pieces to users gracefully.

Anya: Beta gating checklist:
- API spec and example SDK snippets (Sam)
- Runtime DAG executor spike and basic metrics (Liam)
- Streaming event contract + frontend demo (Julie)
- Console opt-in + docs + customer opt-in flow (Maria)
- Evals for race/partial failure cases (Product)

Sam: I'll draft the formal API types and include examples for CLI/SDK by EOD Wed.

Liam: I'll spike the executor (2w) and add a perf note about tail latencies and mitigation strategies (early cutoff, hedging).

Julie: I'll design the streaming event wire format and a simple frontend sketch.

Maria: I'll prepare beta messaging and gating for Dedicated/Private and coordinate with Legal on data flow for parallel calls.

Anya: Any objections to moving this into a PRD draft after Sam posts the spec?

Dev-ci-bot: deployment scheduled: feature/concurrent-invoke -> staging at 2026-04-02T10:00Z :rocket:

Sam: No objections. I'll post the spec draft shortly.

Liam: +1

Maria: +1

Julie: +1

Anya: Thanks everyone. Will follow up with the PRD link and a short demo next week. :+1:
